topic.title: Tabular Foundation Models and Reliable Benchmarking
topic.overview: Tabular learning handles heterogeneous features and datasets whose statistical structure varies widely. The represented work compares trees, deep networks, and in-context foundation models while examining regularization, synthetic pretraining, and model–data selection. Reusable models must accommodate both small datasets and larger collections without assuming image-like structure.
topic.whyItMatters: Performance rankings depend strongly on tuning budgets, validation methods, and ensembling. A living benchmark can reveal when an apparent advance reflects a stronger evaluation protocol or overfitting to validation data.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives address scalable experimentation and performance prediction. Later work develops tabular deep learning, followed by foundation models and maintained benchmarks. Recent models emphasize diverse synthetic tasks and efficient scaling, while analyses examine uncertainty and prior mismatch. These examples support careful task-dependent comparison rather than a blanket claim that one model family replaces all others.
openQuestions: Which synthetic pretraining distributions cover real tabular problems without harmful priors?
How can benchmarks reward progress while limiting repeated validation-set overfitting?
